blocks.text: When a ship's bow rises on a wave, the turbine rotor spinning below deck does not simply rise with it: it pushes sideways on its bearings with a couple that can reach several kilonewton metres. The same effect, from four spinning wheels, shifts load from the inner to the outer wheels of a car in a bend. This unit estimates those loads.

blocks.markdown: A rotor of polar moment of inertia $I$ (kg m$^2$) spinning at angular speed $\omega$ (rad/s) has angular momentum $H=I\omega$ along its spin axis. If the spin axis is turned about a perpendicular axis at **precession** rate $\omega_p$ (rad/s), the direction of $H$ changes, and a torque must act. The bearings supply that torque on the rotor, and the rotor exerts the equal and opposite **gyroscopic reaction couple** on the supports.

blocks.caption: Magnitude of the gyroscopic couple, valid when the spin axis and precession axis are perpendicular. The couple axis is perpendicular to both.

blocks.title: Gyroscopic reaction on supports
blocks.text: The reaction couple on the frame has the magnitude $I\omega\omega_p$. Its axis is perpendicular to both the spin axis and the precession axis. For a rotor on two bearings a distance $\ell$ apart, the couple is carried as equal and opposite forces $\pm C/\ell$ at the bearings (in addition to the static weight).

blocks.markdown: **Ship rotor.** A turbine rotor with its axis along the ship's length pitches (rotates about the transverse axis) as the ship rocks. For harmonic pitching with amplitude $\phi_0$ (rad) and period $T_p$ (s), the angular velocity is $\omega_p=\phi_0(2\pi/T_p)\cos(2\pi t/T_p)$ with maximum $\phi_0\,2\pi/T_p$. The gyroscopic couple therefore acts about a vertical axis, so the bearing reactions are horizontal and sideways, and they oscillate at the pitching period.

blocks.title: Bearing reactions on a pitching ship
blocks.prompt: A rotor ($I=300$ kg m$^2$) turns at 3000 rev/min with its axis along the ship. The ship pitches harmonically with amplitude $6^\circ$ and period 12 s. The bearings are 2.5 m apart. Find the maximum gyroscopic couple and the bearing reactions it produces.

steps.text: Spin speed and maximum precession rate.

blocks.answer: Maximum gyroscopic couple about 5.17 kN m, giving about 2.07 kN at each bearing (opposite in direction) at the extreme of the pitching rate; it falls to zero at the extremes of pitch angle.

blocks.markdown: **Vehicle in a bend.** When a vehicle travels at speed $v$ (m/s) round a curve of radius $R$ (m), the whole car yaws at $\omega_p=v/R$, while each wheel of radius $r$ spins at $\omega=v/r$. All four wheels spin in the same sense, so their gyroscopic couples add: $C=\sum I_w\omega\omega_p$. For a left turn, the reaction couple on the vehicle acts to **raise the inner (left) side** and **press down the outer (right) side**, so the outer wheels carry extra vertical load and the inner wheels lose the same total.

blocks.title: Four wheels in a bend
blocks.prompt: A car with four wheels, each of $I_w=0.8$ kg m$^2$ and radius 0.35 m, takes a bend of radius 60 m at 20 m/s. The track width is 1.5 m. Find the gyroscopic couple and the total change in vertical load between the outer and inner sides.

steps.text: Load transfer across the track width.

blocks.answer: $C=61$ N m and about 41 N of load transfers from the inner to the outer wheels, which is small compared with centrifugal load transfer but grows with $v^2$.

rows: Car or lorry in a bend
Whirl speed shifts with spin speed
blocks.caption: Gyroscopic effects in machines.

blocks.markdown: **Flexible shaft and whirl.** A disc on a flexible shaft whirls (its centre orbits the bearing line) in either the **forward** direction (same sense as spin) or the **backward** direction. If the disc is mounted midway between the bearings, it translates without tilting and the gyroscopic effect is negligible. If it is **overhung**, whirling makes the disc axis tilt, and the gyroscopic moment on the tilted disc resists the tilt. In **forward whirl** this acts like extra stiffness, so the whirl speed (critical speed) rises with the spin speed. In **backward whirl** it acts like reduced stiffness and the whirl speed falls. A polar inertia larger than the transverse inertia (a thin disc) makes the effect strong.

blocks.title: Stability
blocks.text: Gyroscopic stiffening of forward whirl moves the critical speed up, which can make it possible to run a flexible-shaft machine between or above critical speeds. Backward whirl is rarely excited by unbalance, which excites forward whirl, but it can occur through friction or anisotropic supports.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.text: Using rev/min instead of rad/s, taking the precession rate to be the pitching frequency rather than its angular velocity, and assuming the reaction forces at both bearings act in the same direction (they are equal and opposite for a couple).

points: The gyroscopic couple is $C=I\omega\omega_p$; on a two-bearing rotor it gives equal and opposite bearing forces $C/\ell$.
For a car in a bend, $\omega=v/r$ and $\omega_p=v/R$; the reaction couple transfers load to the outer wheels.
In a flexible-shaft rotor, forward whirl stiffens with spin speed (higher critical speed) while backward whirl softens; a mid-span disc is almost unaffected.

questions.stem: A rotor with polar moment of inertia $I$ spins at $\omega$ while its axis precesses at $\omega_p$ about a perpendicular axis. What is the magnitude of the gyroscopic couple?

distractorRationale.b: This has the dimensions of energy, not torque.
distractorRationale.c: This would be a centripetal-type term and ignores the spin.
distractorRationale.d: This adds angular velocities rather than combining them as a cross product.

questions.explanation: The rate of change of angular momentum $\mathbf H=I\boldsymbol\omega$ due to rotation of its direction is $\boldsymbol\omega_p\times\mathbf H$, with magnitude $I\omega\omega_p$ when the axes are perpendicular.

questions.stem: A marine turbine rotor with $I=180$ kg m$^2$ spins at 6000 rev/min. The ship pitches with a maximum angular velocity of 0.04 rad/s about an axis perpendicular to the rotor axis. Find the maximum gyroscopic couple in N m.
A rotor ($I=240$ kg m$^2$) spins at 4500 rev/min in two bearings 2.0 m apart on a ship whose pitching rate reaches 0.05 rad/s. Find the magnitude of the gyroscopic force on each bearing in N.
questions.explanation: $\omega=4500(2\pi)/60=471.2$ rad/s and $C=240(471.2)(0.05)=5655$ N m. A couple on two bearings 2.0 m apart gives forces $\pm C/\ell=\pm2827$ N.

questions.stem: A four-wheeled vehicle has wheels of radius 0.40 m with $I_w=1.2$ kg m$^2$ each. It travels at 25 m/s round a bend of radius 100 m with track width 1.6 m. Considering only the wheels' gyroscopic effect, find the magnitude of the change in vertical reaction on each outer wheel in N (the two outer wheels share the load equally).
questions.explanation: $\omega=25/0.4=62.5$ rad/s and $\omega_p=25/100=0.25$ rad/s, so $C=4(1.2)(62.5)(0.25)=75$ N m. The load transfer is $C/b=75/1.6=46.9$ N spread over two outer wheels, i.e. $23.4$ N each.

questions.stem: A car with four wheels turns left. Considering only the gyroscopic effect of the wheels, how do the vertical wheel reactions change?

options.text: The inner wheels carry more load and the outer wheels less
The outer wheels carry more load and the inner wheels carry less
All four wheel reactions increase equally
The front wheels gain load and the rear wheels lose it

questions.correctOptionText: The outer wheels carry more load and the inner wheels carry less

distractorRationale.a: This is the opposite of the actual reaction couple direction.
distractorRationale.c: A couple changes loads in equal and opposite amounts; it does not alter total weight.
distractorRationale.d: The couple axis is along the direction of travel, so it transfers load across the track, not fore and aft.

questions.explanation: The wheels' angular momentum points along the axle (to the left), and a left turn swings that vector toward the rear. The torque this requires, and the equal and opposite reaction on the car, act about the longitudinal axis; the reaction tends to raise the inner side and press the outer side down.

questions.stem: A rotor's spin speed is doubled and the pitching rate of the ship also doubles. What happens to the gyroscopic couple on the bearings?

distractorRationale.a: The couple is proportional to the product of the two rates, so both factors contribute.
distractorRationale.b: Both rates increase, so the couple must increase.
distractorRationale.d: The couple has only two rate factors, so the multiplier is $2\times2$.

questions.stem: A rotor ($I=95$ kg m$^2$) spins at 9000 rev/min in bearings 1.2 m apart. The vessel pitches harmonically with amplitude $4^\circ$ and period 9 s. Find the maximum force in N at each bearing due to the gyroscopic couple.
questions.explanation: $\omega=942.5$ rad/s and $\omega_{p,\max}=0.069813(2\pi/9)=0.04874$ rad/s. Then $C=95(942.5)(0.04874)=4364$ N m and each bearing force is $C/1.2=3636$ N.

questions.stem: A thin disc is mounted overhung on a flexible shaft and whirls in the same sense as its spin (forward whirl). How does the gyroscopic effect influence its whirl (critical) speed as the spin speed increases?

options.text: It acts as extra stiffness, so the forward-whirl critical speed rises
It acts as reduced stiffness, so the critical speed falls
It has no effect because the disc is symmetric
It makes the shaft unstable at all speeds

questions.correctOptionText: It acts as extra stiffness, so the forward-whirl critical speed rises

distractorRationale.b: That is the effect on backward whirl.
distractorRationale.c: The disc tilts as it whirls and the polar inertia makes the gyroscopic moment significant.
distractorRationale.d: Forward whirl is stiffened rather than destabilised by gyroscopic effects.

questions.explanation: In forward whirl the gyroscopic moment resists tilting of the disc, behaving like added stiffness that increases with spin speed. In backward whirl the moment acts the other way and lowers the whirl speed.

questions.stem: Explain why a disc located at the mid-span of a flexible shaft shows little gyroscopic effect, whereas an overhung disc shows a strong effect. Describe how the effect changes the whirl speeds as spin speed increases.
markingGuide: Mid-span disc translates in whirl without tilting, so the spin axis keeps its direction
Overhung disc tilts as the shaft bends, so its spin axis precesses
Gyroscopic moment $\approx(I_p\omega\omega_{\text{whirl}})$ resists the tilt for forward whirl (stiffening)
Forward whirl speed rises with spin speed, backward whirl speed falls
Effect is larger when polar inertia exceeds transverse inertia
questions.explanation: The gyroscopic moment arises only when the spin axis changes direction. That occurs for the overhung disc because the shaft slope at the disc varies with whirl motion.

questions.stem: Explain how the gyroscopic effect of a car's rotating wheels alters wheel loads when it takes a bend, giving the expression for the couple and saying how it varies with vehicle speed. Compare its size qualitatively with the effect of centrifugal force.
markingGuide: Couple $C=\sum I_w\omega\omega_p=\sum I_w v^2/(rR)$, proportional to $v^2$ and inversely to $R$
Reaction couple tends to raise the inner side and press down the outer side
Load transfer $\Delta R=C/b$ with track width $b$
Centrifugal (inertial) overturning moment $mv^2h/R$ is much larger because $mh\gg\sum I_w/r$, though both scale with $v^2/R$
questions.explanation: Both effects scale with $v^2/R$ but the centrifugal term involves the whole vehicle mass acting at the height of its centre of mass, so it dominates in practice.
